newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco deploys forces at Islamist students trial.
newsitem.headline: Morocco deploys forces at Islamist students trial.

text.p: Morocco authorities on Thursday deployed police forces around a Casablanca building where three Moslem fundamentalist students were being tried, eyewitnesses said.
"The forces were put out to quell any possible unrest," an eyewitness said.

The three students, members of the outlawed fundamentalist al-Adl wal Ihsane (Justice and Charity) group, were arrested recently in Casablanca after unrest in the campus over transport problems, a student union spokesman said.
They are charged with "disturbing order and aggression against a civil servant," lawyers said. It was not clear what penalty they face.
Al-Adl wal Ihsane group was banned in 1990. Its leader, Abdsalam Yassine, has been under house arrest since December 1989 in Sale, the twin city of Rabat.
Another 27 students under arrest are expected to appear before a Casablanca court next week on similar charges, the student spokesman said.
